body.statement: For fixed \(K\) and \(b\), every rational table satisfying \(0\le r_{q,a}\le q\), including tables with boundary entries or a treated-count menu constant in \(a\), every rational contrast \(c\), and every size profile \(s\), \(R^\star\) is unchanged when nature is restricted to binary schedules. Every endpoint estimator table \(d\) has the multilinear extension \(\overline d\) from \(\texttt{def:endpoint-extension}\) with \(\sup_{Y\in\mathcal M}\mathcal R(D,\overline d;Y)\le\max_{Y\in\mathcal M\cap\{0,1\}^{2KN}}\mathcal R(D,d;Y)\). Moreover, invariant procedures and priors reduce the unrestricted game exactly to \(\operatorname{val}(\mathsf P)=\operatorname{val}(\mathsf Q)=R^\star\), with rational kernel \(H\), attainment, a posterior-mean endpoint rule on positive-mass cells, arbitrary clipped values on zero-mass cells, and an implementable correlated design obtained from assignment histograms followed by the conditional uniform sampling of \(\texttt{lem:conditional-uniformity}\). The orbit data have at most \((m+1)^{O(2^{2Kb}+K2^b)}\) entries.
body.justification: This is the lossless finite reduction for every feasible exact-count menu, including pure-control, pure-treatment, and label-constant menus, while retaining the full observation hypergraph.
body.gap: SudijonoDobribanTchetgenTchetgen2026 and Hull2026 obtain endpoint reductions for no interference, while KandirosHarshawSavje2026 bounds a graph-indexed network game; none gives an exact polynomial-size orbit game for a non-pairwise exact-count observation hypergraph.
body.consumer: BairdBohrenMcIntoshOzler2018's saturation shares can be chosen against exact bounded-schedule risk while simultaneously selecting a nonlinear analysis rule.
